body:
tanya: Welcome aboard @oliver! Quick question from recruitment: your start date is Dec 28 which overlaps our mandatory year-end shutdown. Do we require new hires to take unpaid time if they haven't accrued PTO yet?
oliver: Hi all 3 I'm trying to plan travel. I start on 12/28 and my offer shows standard accrual starting day 1. I won't have many earned days by year-end though. Do I need to be off unpaid for 12/29-1/2?
mike: Oliver will be attached to my team. Our understanding was new hires start accruing immediately, but company blackout expects everyone to be off. Curious about payroll mechanics here.
peopleops: Short answer: new hires accrue PTO from the first day, but usable balance for the immediate year depends on the prorated accrual schedule. For hires starting during the shutdown we typically allow one of these options: 1) If the offer included paid holidays/backpay clauses we can mark those shutdown days as paid; 2) Convert to 1-2 days of advance PTO (manager + People Ops approval) to cover the gap; 3) If neither applies, the days are unpaid.
peopleops: Policy excerpt:
````
New Hire Year-End Guidance (excerpt):
- Accrual begins on start date.
- Company shutdown days are paid for employees with an active paid status on their start date unless the offer letter states otherwise.
- Managers can request an advance PTO exception (up to 5 days) for a new hire if the accrual schedule would otherwise leave them unpaid during a mandatory shutdown.
````
tanya: Oliver's offer doesn't call out special holiday pay. Mike can you confirm if the team budget has room for an advance PTO exception?
mike: We can absorb up to 2 days as advance PTO. If more needed, People Ops please advise.
oliver: Thanks 3 I'd prefer advance PTO to avoid unpaid gaps. I'll happily sign an acknowledgement to repay any negative balance if I leave within 6 months.
peopleops: Good note. For advance PTO we'll need manager approval (confirmed), candidate acknowledgement signed, and People Ops ticket filed: https://intranet.redwood/hr/forms/advance-pto. Payroll-bot will annotate the hire so year-end shutdown isn't auto-marked unpaid.
payroll-bot: automated note: to prevent unpaid designation, People Ops must submit payroll annotation before payroll cutoff (2025-12-15 17:00 PT).
peopleops: Tanya 3 please have Oliver sign the acknowledgement and I'll submit the payroll annotation. Expect confirmation within 48 hours of submission.
oliver: Signing now. Appreciate the fast help.
tanya: Thanks everyone, closing loop once payroll confirms. :white_check_mark:
